bib.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era

question: Can an RNN be trained in parallel like a transformer, scaled to billions of parameters, and match similarly sized transformers while keeping constant-memory, linear-time inference?
hypothesis: A linear-attention formulation with channel-wise time decay (RWKV) can combine parallel transformer-style training with RNN inference and perform on par with transformers of the same size and compute.
contributions: The introduction of RWKV, a novel architecture combining RNNs and Transformer advantages while mitigating their limitations.
Detailed experiments demonstrating RWKV's performance and efficiency on benchmark datasets for large-scale models.
The release of pretrained models, from 169 million to 14 billion parameters, trained on the Pile.

method.summary: RWKV stacks residual blocks of time-mixing (an AFT-like WKV operator with a per-channel decay w and current-token bonus u, plus token shift and sigmoid receptance gating) and channel-mixing (squared ReLU). It runs in time-parallel mode for training and as an RNN for inference. Six models (169M to 14B) were trained one epoch on the Pile (330B tokens) and compared FLOP-matched with Pythia, OPT and BLOOM.
method.task: next-token pretraining of a language model; zero-shot NLP benchmarks; long-context finetuning; LRA

training.objective: cross-entropy next-token plus PaLM auxiliary loss pushing the softmax normalizer toward zero
training.optimizer: Adam, betas (0.9, 0.99) (printed as epsilon), no weight decay
training.lr_schedule: constant for warmup mini-epochs, then exponential decay to End LR at the last mini-epoch
training.warmup: constant LR for 361/411/443/451/465/544 mini-epochs (169M/430M/1.5B/3B/7B/14B); mini-epoch = 40320 samples
training.batch_size: dynamically switched between 128 or 256 sequences of 1024 tokens
training.compute: compute budget in exaFLOP shown only on figure axes (about 1e2 to 1e3)

other.init: embeddings U(+-1e-4), most weights zero, no biases (App. E)

inference.prompting: zero-shot on LM benchmarks; Raven comparisons use prompts chosen for ChatGPT, then a re-ordered RWKV-adapted version

other.speed benchmark: float32, HuggingFace Transformers, CPU x86 and NVIDIA A100 80GB, all parameters counted

evidence.quote: we use ϵ = (0.9, 0.99) without weight decay for the Adam optimizer

results.claim: RWKV scales to 14B parameters, trained for one epoch on the Pile.
results.quote: We scale our models as large as 14 billion parameters, by far the largest dense RNN ever trained

results.claim: Loss vs compute follows a transformer-style scaling law; Pareto-optimal linear fit has r2 0.994.
results.setup: 45 RWKV models over (dataset, parameters) pairs, loss vs exaFLOP
results.quote: the linear fit to the Pareto optimal points holding an r2 value of 0.994

results.claim: Extrapolating the fit one more order of magnitude of compute gives r2 0.875.
results.setup: same scaling-law fit, extrapolated one order of magnitude
results.quote: we find an extremely good fit with an r2 of 0.875

results.claim: RWKV is competitive with Pythia, OPT and BLOOM on a FLOP-matched basis across twelve zero-shot tasks (read from figures, no table of numbers).
results.setup: 169M-14B RWKV vs Pythia/OPT/BLOOM; one Pile epoch of 330B tokens; ARC, BoolQ, COPA, HeadQA, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, OBQA, PIQA, ReCoRD, SciQ, Winogrande; zero-shot

results.claim: RTE F1 Macro for Raven-14B rises from 44.2 to 74.8 when the prompt is re-ordered.
results.setup: RWKV-4-Raven-14B, zero-shot RTE, ChatGPT prompt vs re-ordered RWKV prompt

results.claim: ChatGPT scores 88.1 F1 Macro on RTE with the same prompt used for RWKV-GPT (44.2).
results.setup: RTE, zero-shot, prompts chosen for ChatGPT

results.claim: Raven-14B reaches 5.43% on MathQA with chain-of-thought and 4.13% without; ChatGPT 71.40.
results.quote: the Raven model achieved a very low accuracy of 5.43%

results.claim: Raven-14B beats ChatGPT on sarcasm detection (50.96 vs 49.88 F1 Macro) but trails SOTA 53.57.
results.note: Table 7 SOTA column for Sarcasm is 53.57; the Unhealthy SOTA is 50.96, same digits.

results.claim: LRA average accuracy of RWKV is 72.07 versus S4 86.09; RWKV fails Path-X and scores 58.42 on Pathfinder.
results.setup: Long Range Arena, six tasks; baselines cited from Gu et al. 2022 and Alam et al. 2023
results.note: Text says 'second only to S4 in five datasets'.

results.claim: Enwik8: RWKV-RNN2 (12 layers, d=512, T=1024) test bpc 1.178 vs 1.137 for the 12-layer Transformer.
results.setup: Enwik8, L=12, d=512, T=1024; RWKV-RNN2 trained with AdamW wd 0.1, dropout 0.1, batch 16, lr 6e-4 per footnote
results.table: Table 5, row RWKV-RNN2, column Test bpc
results.note: RWKV-RNN1 (6 layers) train bpc 0.720, no test bpc reported.

results.claim: Context extension: 1024 to 2048 (10B tokens), 4096 (100B), 8192 (100B); Pile test loss falls with context length.
results.setup: RWKV 7B and 14B, finetuning on the Pile

results.claim: Per-token inference time and memory are O(Td) time overall and O(d) space; cumulative generation time grows linearly with length, unlike transformers.
results.setup: float32, HuggingFace Transformers, CPU x86 and A100 80GB, vs Bloom, OPT, GPT-Neo, Pythia

results.claim: RWKV per-layer state is 5DL numbers (4DL without the helper exponent).

limits: Linear attention funnels information through one vector, which may hurt recall of minutiae over very long contexts (Limitations).
Prompt engineering matters more than for transformers; prompt order nearly doubled RTE F1.
Competitiveness shown on FLOP-matched benchmarks via figures only; no numeric benchmark table, no seeds or error bars.
Hardware, GPU count and wall clock for pretraining are not stated.
LRA: far below S4 on Image, Pathfinder, Path-X.
Raven instruction-tuning details are not given.
Raven MathQA accuracy was very low (5.43%).
